summary.en: A combined British, French and Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet in Navarino Bay. The engagement was not intended as a battle and no power had declared war. It nonetheless ended Ottoman capacity to hold the Peloponnese by sea and made Greek independence a question of terms rather than of outcome.

body_html.en:
The Treaty of London of July 1827 committed Britain, France and Russia to impose an armistice on both sides. Ibrahim Pasha refused to stop operations in the Morea, and Codrington took the allied squadrons into Navarino Bay on 20 October to make the blockade felt.

A musket shot at a British boat set off a general action at anchor. Within a few hours about sixty Ottoman and Egyptian ships had been sunk or burned, against no allied losses. The Sultan's ability to supply Ibrahim was gone. It was the last fleet action fought entirely under sail, and the decisive act of the war.
